what_happened: A docs job to build the Olympus spec layer (docs/spec.toml, a checking test, a changelog entry and a decision record) was rejected at final verification. The verifier did not finish: it hit its 1200-second deadline. All 7 acceptance criteria are listed as unmet, but none was shown to be wrong. No findings and no failed checks are listed, so nothing says whether the work was good. The job was large: it covered requirements across Olympus sections 1-10, the governing philosophy and the addenda, with verbatim quotes and four negative test cases.
cause: The verifier runs under one fixed time limit whatever the job's size, and its work grows with the number of criteria. It must run the full test suite, clippy and fmt, and also check many quotes against BRIEF.md. Nothing scales the limit, orders the cheap checks first, or saves a verdict per criterion as it is reached. A timeout is therefore recorded as a plain fail with every criterion unmet. Nothing separates "not judged" from "judged and failed", so the rejection says nothing about the work and the whole job is wasted. Planning also does not bound how much verification work a job creates.
prevention: Make a verifier timeout a distinct outcome, "unjudged", not a rejection. Have the verifier record each criterion's verdict as soon as it is reached, and run the repo checks (test, clippy, fmt) once and share the results. On a timeout, keep the partial verdicts and automatically re-run the verifier on only the criteria not yet judged, with a fresh deadline. Also scale the deadline with the number of criteria, or have the critic flag jobs whose verification looks too large for one window.
proposed_request: When the verifier reaches its time deadline, Athena should not reject the job with every criterion unmet. Record the outcome as "verifier timed out, not judged", separate from a real failure. The verifier should save each criterion's verdict as soon as it reaches one, and run the repo checks (cargo test, clippy, fmt) once and share the results. After a timeout, Athena should keep the saved verdicts and re-run the verifier on only the unjudged criteria with a fresh deadline, up to a set number of attempts. Then re-run job 20261018-120736-90w3 (the Olympus spec layer in docs/spec.toml) and show it gets a real verdict. Demonstrate with a test that uses a fake verifier that times out part-way: the partial verdicts are kept, the retry covers only the rest, and the final outcome is not recorded as a rejection of all criteria.
